result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both are compact, festival-specific confirmation cards that read clearly. A leaves the unknown facts as plainly marked blanks ([add details here], [volunteer contact link]). B states things the brief never gave: that a confirmation email was sent, that you can reply to it, and to wear comfortable shoes and a warm layer. A's 'change or cancel' link assumes a feature exists, and both pages have a generic 'Back to the festival' button plus a secondary link instead of one clear volunteer action. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both are small, single-card pages that are clearly about volunteering for a lantern festival and stay readable. A makes up details the brief never gave: a confirmation email you can reply to, and advice to wear comfortable shoes and bring a warm layer. B leaves the date, meeting place and contact as clearly marked blanks. B loses a little because it adds a second action, a 'Change or cancel your sign-up' link the brief didn't mention, but it is still the better answer on not inventing facts.
